title: Aston Villa’s Alysson suffers adductor issue, his fourth injury since signing
content:
Aston Villa winger Alysson is facing a race against time to be fit before the end of the season, having recently suffered an adductor injury in training.

The 19-year-old signed from Brazilian side Gremio in January and in a deal worth €12million ($14m; £10.5m), plus a 10 per cent sell-on clause.

However, Alysson has only made three Premier League appearances, with regular injuries limiting his involvement under Unai Emery.

The wide player picked up a knee injury in his first couple of training sessions in January, delaying his debut for a month, before suffering another muscle issue in March, before suffering another issue in February and then a groin problem in March, ruling him out for three weeks.

Alysson has not played for Villa since coming on for the final 27 minutes of Villa’s 4-1 home defeat against Chelsea in March. He was also not included in Villa’s Europa League squad, with the club only allowed to make three alterations ahead of the knockout phase, with January signings Tammy Abraham and Douglas Luiz, plus the return of Leon Bailey, included.

The latest setback is a thigh issue, once again sustained in training. There is a hope from sources close to the player, speaking on the condition of anonymity, that he could be an option for Emery in time for the final week of Villa’s season, where they will travel to Manchester City.
